youtube.title: 16 Colors You'll Never See #shorts
youtube.description:
There's a color you can't see. The mantis shrimp perceives 16 color receptors while humans only have 3, meaning they see an entirely alien spectrum of hues that exist in the ocean but are literally invisible to your brain.

Your eyes capture light and send signals to your brain, which interprets them as colors. But your brain can only process combinations of red, green, and blue light. The mantis shrimp's visual system operates on a completely different wavelength—literally. With 12 to 16 types of photoreceptor cells (compared to our measly 3), these crustaceans don't blend colors the way we do. They see ultraviolet, visible light, and polarized light all at once, in dimensions we can't even conceptualize.

Imagine trying to explain "blue" to someone who's only ever seen red and yellow. That's us trying to understand mantis shrimp vision. Their superpower isn't just about seeing more—it's about perceiving reality in a way that fundamentally differs from ours. In the ocean depths where they live, this vision gives them a predatory advantage we can barely fathom.
